about: The frontier: text for the nine location beats the game only named, the unlock quests, cargo cults and proto-Hatters at the outposts, the ruins, the megastructure, the Lyra rumour and the cult world past the portal. Nobody here meets an alien, though plenty of people use the word.

grey_hats.name: The Grey Hats
grey_hats.about: an outpost hacker crew; proto-Hatters; clean records for a fee

scar_tribe.name: The Star-Shaped Scar Tribe
scar_tribe.about: cargo cult at Zeta Reticuli; wear an old Earth star map as ritual marks

kettle_survivor.name: Ottilie Brandt
kettle_survivor.about: survivor of the hauler Maud Kettle, lost in Lyra; tells the story for drinks

tarnished_gear.name: Order of the Tarnished Gear
tarnished_gear.about: cargo cult that collects broken technology; sells the working kind cheap, out of distaste

worshipped.about: the Tarnished Gear adopted the captain's ship as a minor relic

grey_hats_client.about: the captain paid the Grey Hats to clean a record

heard_the_lyra_story.about: the captain heard how the Maud Kettle went down in Lyra

logged_the_lyra_signal.about: the captain copied the Lyra signal log at the research outpost

hatters.grey.title: The Grey Hats
hatters.grey.text: A crew calling itself the Grey Hats offers to clean your debt record. For a little more they will clean your rivals' records too, by which they mean fill them.

choices.say: Keep your record as it is

zeta.cult.title: The waiting city
zeta.cult.text: Zeta Reticuli is home to the Star-Shaped Scar Tribe. Their founders came here because an old Earth story put Zeta Reticuli at the centre of a star map, and they wear that map as ritual marks. They waited for someone to come and meet them. Nobody did, so now they meet every ship themselves, at the dock, with a brass band.

megastructure.stator.title: The Stator Field
megastructure.stator.text: Out past Sedna the segments hang in a line that bends round the Sun. Each is the size of a hauler. Every eleven hours they turn together, a few degrees, though nothing connects them that your instruments can find.

builder.beacon.title: The beacon
builder.beacon.text: The segment Scholz's Star pulled away still turns, alone, and on its rim the builders left a beacon. It points away from every human route, at a patch of sky with nothing in it. {ancient_scholar.short}, when you tell her, corrects you: nothing yet.

ruins.alpha.title: Foundations in the ice
ruins.alpha.text: Under forty metres of comet ice in Tau Ceti's debris disk: foundations, cut square, in the grey alloy. The ice above them is younger than the foundations by a long way. Whatever stood on them was taken away carefully.

ruins.beta.title: The anchor
ruins.beta.text: On a moon of Epsilon Indi's cold giant, a ring of pylons sunk into the bedrock, all leaning the same way. {ancient_scholar.short}'s notes call it an anchor. Her notes do not say what it anchored.

signal.lyra.title: Not proven
signal.lyra.text: The outpost's dish points at Lyra. Every few weeks it logs a burst of magnetic chirps from somewhere past HD 178911: structured, repeating, and not radio. Someone has written ALIEN on the whiteboard. Someone else has crossed it out and written NOT PROVEN. A third hand has added a smiley face.

rumour.lyra.title: How the Maud Kettle went down
text: {kettle_survivor} tells the bar how the Maud Kettle went down in Lyra, out past HD 178911. Near one moon of a big gas giant the electronics went soft: screens melted into noise, the navigation computer counted backwards, the coffee machine prayed.
They flew home on a sextant and a wind-up watch. 'Something on that moon answered our radio,' she says. 'In magnetic pulses.' Nobody buys the next round, so she buys it herself.

builder.crossing.title: The segment turns
text: Close up, the segment the star stole turns faster than anything that old should. {ancient_scholar.short} watches the readings and says nothing for a long time.
Then: 'It is a door. It does not care which way we go through.'

unlock.AsteroidBase.text: Survey drones report mining in places no claim was ever filed: Tau Ceti's debris disk, the moons of Epsilon Indi's cold giant, the collision belt at Fomalhaut. Somebody is working rock off the books.

unlock.DeepSpaceOutpost.text: The brown dwarfs between the stars make good fuel stops if somebody guards them: Luhman 16, WISE 0855, Scholz's Star. The outposts want a few escort runs before they open to traffic.

unlock.ResearchColony.text: Three research colonies need a hauler who understands priority cargo: Nova Labs at Wolf 359, the Quantum Center at YZ Ceti and the Stellar Institute, far out at TRAPPIST-1.

beat.AsteroidBase.mineral_discovery.title: A seam of heavy metal
beat.AsteroidBase.mineral_discovery.text: The survey drone finds a seam of iridium and osmium. The base's assayer says it is exactly what haulers would want for coinage, if haulers had coinage. The quartermaster says it is exactly what pays for a new air plant.

beat.AsteroidBase.pirate_hideout.title: Closed for raiding
beat.AsteroidBase.pirate_hideout.text: A cave in the rock has been fitted with a docking ring, a bar and a hand-painted sign: CLOSED FOR RAIDING. BACK SOON.

beat.AsteroidBase.ancient_technology.title: Old metal
beat.AsteroidBase.ancient_technology.text: A miner shows you a shard of grey alloy cut from a comet core. It blunted the drill that found it. Under magnification the edges are machined.

beat.DeepSpaceOutpost.smuggler_network.title: The second price list
beat.DeepSpaceOutpost.smuggler_network.text: Every outpost has a second price list. This one keeps it printed on the back of the first, to save paper.

beat.DeepSpaceOutpost.alien_contact.title: First contact
beat.DeepSpaceOutpost.alien_contact.text: The outpost belongs to the Cult of the Broken Machine, founded by the crew of a hauler that broke down here forty years ago. They worship that hauler and leave it offerings of technology, which it ignores. They would like to worship yours as well, part-time.
notes: was 'Alien contact' with no text: Cargo has no aliens to contact

beat.DeepSpaceOutpost.trade_revolution.title: Priced by weight
beat.DeepSpaceOutpost.trade_revolution.text: The outpost traders have started pricing everything by how much iridium it would buy, by the gram. They call the unit a mark. Nobody owns the idea yet.

beat.ResearchColony.breakthrough_discove.title: A date for the metal
beat.ResearchColony.breakthrough_discove.text: The colony's physicists have dated the builders' alloy by the decay in its lattice. It was last heated about seventy thousand years ago, which is when Scholz's Star passed the Sun.

beat.ResearchColony.experiment_crisis.title: A humming crate
beat.ResearchColony.experiment_crisis.text: An experiment has gone wrong and the colony would like it moved out of the system. It is in a crate. The crate is humming. The colony pays in advance, which is never a good sign.

beat.ResearchColony.alien_artifacts.title: The builders' metal
beat.ResearchColony.alien_artifacts.text: The colony keeps its sample of the alloy in a glass case with a handwritten card: NOT ALIEN. PROBABLY. The second word was added later, in different ink.

merchant_visit.1.title: Unholy shelf
merchant_visit.1.text: A collector of the Order of the Tarnished Gear buys broken technology: your burnt-out fuel pump, a cracked visor, the coffee machine that only makes hot water. Working things go on the Order's unholy shelf at low prices. On it today: a working fuel pump for your model, out of stock everywhere else.
